# Established findings — `sqlparse.split()` behaviour (derived black-box from `/workspace/dataset/test2_executable`)

These facts are CONFIRMED by running the reference executable. Treat them as ground truth
and build on them; do not re-derive them. Anything not listed here is still unknown.

## Program shape

`main()` parses `--a` (type=str, required) with Python `argparse`, then
`print(sqlparse.split(args.a))` — i.e. it prints the **Python `repr` of a list of `str`**.

Confirmed CLI behaviour:
- `--a VALUE` and `--a=VALUE` both work.
- Missing `--a` → usage line + error on **stderr**, exit code **2**.
- `-h` / `--help` → help text on stdout, exit code 0. Help text is:
  ```
  usage: test2_executable [-h] --a A

  options:
    -h, --help  show this help message and exit
    --a A
  ```
  (the harness normalises the program name, so emit your own program name)
- Empty input `--a ""` → prints `[]`.

## Output formatting

Python list repr: `[` + items joined with `, ` + `]`; `[]` when empty.
Each item is a Python string repr: prefer `'...'`; switch to `"..."` only when the string
contains `'` **and** does not contain `"`. Escape `\\`, the chosen quote, and control
characters (`\n`, `\r`, `\t`, `\xNN`, `\uXXXX`, `\UXXXXXXXX`) exactly as CPython does.

## Splitting model (the important part)

`split()` returns `[str(stmt).strip() for stmt in statements]`, where statements come from a
token-stream splitter. Trailing statements that consist **only of whitespace** are dropped
(`--a "   "` → `[]`), but a statement that strips to `''` is otherwise never produced.

Splitter state: `level` (paren-ish nesting), `beginDepth`, `inCase`, `inDeclare`, `isCreate`,
`consumeWs`, plus the accumulating token list.

Per token, in order:
1. If `consumeWs` is set and the token is **not** whitespace-proper and **not** a
   single-line comment → **emit** the accumulated statement and reset all state.
   IMPORTANT: a *newline* token does NOT count as whitespace here (sqlparse lexes
   `\r\n` / `\r` / `\n` as a distinct `Newline` token type), so a newline after `;`
   terminates the statement, while spaces/tabs do not.
   A single-line comment (`--…` / `# …`, including its trailing newline) IS absorbed,
   so `SELECT 1; -- t\nSELECT 2` → `['SELECT 1; -- t', 'SELECT 2']`.
   A multi-line comment `/*…*/` is NOT absorbed → it starts the next statement.
2. `level += changeSplitLevel(tokenType, value)`:
   - Punctuation `(` → `+1`, `)` → `-1`
   - Non-keyword tokens → `0`
   - `unified = value.toUpperCase()`:
     - `DECLARE` when `isCreate && beginDepth === 0` → `inDeclare = true`, `+1`
     - `BEGIN` → `beginDepth += 1`; returns `+1` when `isCreate`, else `0`
     - `END` → if `!inCase` then `beginDepth = max(0, beginDepth - 1)`, else `inCase = false`; returns `-1`
     - `IF` / `FOR` / `WHILE` / `CASE` when `isCreate && beginDepth > 0` → (`CASE` sets `inCase = true`) `+1`
     - `END IF` / `END FOR` / `END WHILE` → `-1`
     - `CREATE` / `CREATE OR REPLACE` → `isCreate = true`, `0`
     - otherwise `0`
3. Append the token to the current statement.
4. If the token is `;` **and** `level <= 0` **and** `beginDepth === 0` → set `consumeWs`.
   (The `beginDepth === 0` requirement is confirmed: `BEGIN x )); SELECT 1;` is a single
   statement even though `level` is negative there.)
5. `GO` (see below) splits **unconditionally** — regardless of `level` and `beginDepth`.

At end of input, emit the accumulated statement unless it is whitespace-only.

### The BEGIN pre-scan rule (confirmed, unusual)

A `BEGIN` keyword only opens a block (only bumps `beginDepth`) when the next token after it
— **skipping whitespace, newlines AND comments of both kinds** — is not `;`.

Confirmed: `BEGIN;`, `BEGIN ;`, `BEGIN\t;`, `BEGIN /*c*/;`, `BEGIN --c\n;` all split at that
`;`, whereas `BEGIN x;`, `BEGIN 1;`, `BEGIN 'x';`, `BEGIN _x;`, `BEGIN foo;`, `BEGIN\nSELECT 1;`
and `BEGIN -- c\nSELECT 1;` do not. `SELECT 1 BEGIN; SELECT 2;` also splits, so the rule is
positional-independent (it is about what follows `BEGIN`, not about the statement content).

### Multi-word keyword tokens (confirmed)

The lexer emits some multi-word forms as a SINGLE keyword token, which changes `unified` and
therefore the level logic:
- `BEGIN TRANSACTION`, `BEGIN WORK`, `BEGIN DEFERRED TRANSACTION`, `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`
  → single token, so `unified !== 'BEGIN'` → no block opened → the following `;` splits.
  But `BEGIN ATOMIC` is NOT such a form: `BEGIN ATOMIC SELECT 1; SELECT 2;` is one statement.
  (The exact accepted word set still needs probing.)
- `END IF` is a single token: `CREATE PROCEDURE p AS BEGIN IF x THEN NULL; END IF; END; SELECT 1`
  → `['CREATE … END IF; END;', 'SELECT 1']`.
- `END CASE` is NOT a single token (`END` + `CASE` separately) — confirmed via
  `CREATE PROCEDURE p AS BEGIN CASE WHEN x THEN NULL; END CASE; END; SELECT 1` being ONE statement.
- `CREATE OR REPLACE` is a single token and still sets `isCreate`.

### Keyword vs. name (confirmed)

- An identifier immediately followed by `(` is lexed as a **Name**, not a keyword:
  `BEGIN(SELECT 1); SELECT 2;` splits, because `BEGIN` became a Name.
- An identifier immediately **after a `.`** is a Name: `SELECT t.begin; SELECT 2` splits.
- A quoted identifier is never a keyword: `SELECT "BEGIN"; SELECT 2` splits.
- Plain `SELECT begin, 1; SELECT 2` → one statement (lowercase `begin` IS the keyword;
  matching is case-insensitive).

### `GO` splitter (confirmed)

- Case-**sensitive**: `GO` splits; `go`, `gO`, `Go` do not. `GO2` / `GOTO` do not.
- `GO 2` is a single token and stays with the preceding statement:
  `SELECT 1\nGO 2\nSELECT 2` → `['SELECT 1\nGO 2', 'SELECT 2']`.
- It splits at any nesting: `SELECT (1 GO 2)` → `['SELECT (1 GO 2', ')']`,
  `BEGIN GO SELECT 1;` → `['BEGIN GO', 'SELECT 1;']`.
- After `GO`, the same `consumeWs` absorption applies.

### Strings / comments / quoting (confirmed)

- `'…'` with `''` doubling **and** backslash escapes: `SELECT 'a\'; b'; SELECT 2` keeps the
  `;` inside the literal, but `SELECT 'esc\'; SELECT 2` ends the literal at that quote
  (i.e. regex-style backtracking: prefer the escape, fall back to closing the literal so the
  literal can terminate).
- `"…"` behaves the same way (`""` doubling + backslash escapes).
- Backtick `` `…` `` quoting works.
- `[…]` bracket quoting works, but only when `[` is NOT preceded by a word character or `]`:
  `SELECT [a;b];` keeps the `;`, `SELECT a[1;2];` does not.
- Dollar quoting: `$$…$$` and `$tag$…$tag$` hide `;`.
- Prefixed literals `E'…'`, `N'…'`, `U&'…'`, `X'0;1'` all hide `;` (the prefix is a separate
  token; the quoted part still lexes as a string).
- Single-line comments: `--…` needs no space; `#` requires a **following space** —
  `SELECT 1 #cmt; still` splits at the `;` (so `#cmt` is not a comment), while
  `SELECT 1 # cmt; still` does not.
- Unterminated `'…` and `/*…` swallow the rest of the input (no split).

## Tooling available to you

- `node /workspace/harness/probe.mjs --inline '["sql1","sql2"]'` — shows the reference
  executable's exact stdout/stderr/exit code (JSON-escaped) for each input. Avoids all shell
  quoting pain. Entries may also be arrays of raw argv, e.g. `[["-h"]]`.
- `node /workspace/harness/probe.mjs /path/corpus.json` — same, from a file.
- `node /workspace/harness/compare.mjs /path/corpus.json` — differential test of
  `/output/test2.mjs` against the executable; prints every mismatch, exits non-zero on failure.
- `/workspace/corpus/seed.json` — the confirmed corpus behind this document.

Never run `python`; the executable is the only oracle. Do not attempt to unpack or decompile
it — this is a black-box reimplementation.
